Subject: Forecast categories refresh + mandatory pipeline hygiene session

Team,

We're rolling out an update to the forecast category definitions that will take effect immediately for Q3 planning. Finance needs a clean, consistent view of what counts as Commit vs Best Case vs Pipeline — this will feed into next quarter's capacity and spend planning. Please do the following by end of week (EOW):

- Update every open opportunity in your book to the new category definitions (see attached PDF).
- Run the attached pipeline audit template on any deals > $100k and upload the completed sheet to the Drive folder linked below.
- Attend one mandatory 45-min calibration session next week (invite and options attached).

Quick summary of the key changes (short version):
- Commit: Deal has signed intent (SOW or PO), pricing agreed, and legal has cleared core terms. Probability = 90%. Use Commit only when there is a clear procurement trigger and finance can reasonably expect cash in the quarter. Example: renewal with signed PO.
- Best Case: Sales confident and champion confirmed, commercial terms substantially agreed but either legal or procurement still outstanding OR close date is at risk by > 1 week. Probability = 60%.
- Pipeline: Early-stage conversations, discovery or evaluation, or deals dependent on customer budget cycles not yet confirmed. Probability = 25%.

We're instituting a weekly commit review: every Monday 11:00am PT we'll run a short sync between Sales Leadership and FP&A to validate Commit-line items. I will circulate the first agenda ahead of Monday.

Attachments: forecast_definitions_v2.pdf, pipeline-audit-template.xlsx, training_invite.ics
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cForecastDocs
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/record/DEAL-7890

Thanks — this will sharply reduce forecast variance and help us size Dedicated capacity properly.

—

Thanks — answering the two points from Aditya and the Acme note: 

- Multi-year deals with a verbal CFO approval but no PO: unless there is a signed commercial agreement or a customer PO we should treat as Best Case. The exception is when there is a binding signed intent (SOW/LOI) that finance accepts as sufficient; those can be Commit but only after FP&A sign-off. For clarity: Commit requires (A) commercial terms agreed, (B) procurement trigger (PO or signed SOW/LOI), and (C) legal has cleared core terms OR FP&A has explicitly approved the risk.

- Partner-led deals: customer-side PO is sufficient for Commit if the partner contract does not introduce additional contingencies. If partner signature is required for revenue recognition in that account, then wait for partner contract. We'll document partner-specific rules in the partner playbook.

I've attached a short 'decision checklist' to the Drive (also copied into the forecast PDF). For operationalizing: we'll run the first Commit review on Mon 15 Jun, 11:00am PT. Marissa is setting up the calendar and will share the dial-in.
